instrument: xml clause 3 — the references-12 refusal, measured against the corpus instead of asserted from a label
question: The bar accepts a refused claim only if the refusal is itself evidenced. The 12 edges the gate counts `unresolved` on `references` are class `unresolved` (X13) in the analyzer. Do their targets name anything the corpus holds — and if they do, is the refusal wrong?

method.audit: the whole-population census classifies every edge against its OWN PROJECT's key space and then re-checks every `unresolved` name against a POOLED key space built from all 126 repositories, so 'held nowhere' means every repository, not one.
method.scopeNote: the audit is CLAIM-BLIND and therefore wider than the gate's 277 residual: it lists every edge naming nothing published in its project (2,995), of which the gate counts 277 because the rest now carry verified/unverifiable external claims.

theTwelve.allTwelveAre: `entity_reference` edges — `ř` `í` `–` `“` `”` `°` `&qandasetbody;` `&stress;` `&woohoo;` `&mindefault;` `&maxdefault;` — in libxslt's and otp's deliberately-malformed test documents
theTwelve.publishedSymbolsHeldNowhere: 12 of 12 — no repository PUBLISHES a symbol of any of these names
theTwelve.sourceDeclarationsExistInTheCorpus: 11 of 12 — measured by searching the corpus source for `<!ENTITY <name>`:

declaredIn.qandasetbody: libxslt/tests/docbook/test/qa.xml ITSELF, in its internal DTD subset (line 4)

declaredNowhere.woohoo: no `<!ENTITY woohoo` anywhere in the corpus — genuinely unresolvable

ruling.theRefusalIsCorrectAndNowEvidenceBacked: For 11 of the 12 the declaration EXISTS in the corpus — in the same repository, in the DTD/entity file the document's DOCTYPE points at. An `isExternalTarget` claim says 'the declaration this target names is not in the population', which would be FALSE for those 11. AND THE GATE WOULD STILL VERIFY IT, because `verifyExternalClaim` looks the name up in the PUBLISHED SYMBOL key space and a DTD entity declaration is not published as a symbol. Claiming these edges would therefore not merely be unmeasured — it would be a false statement the gate certifies. That is the strongest form the refusal could take, and it is the opposite of the laundering the bar warns about.
ruling.forWoohoo: 1 of 12 is declared nowhere in the corpus, so a claim on it alone would be true; it is refused for uniformity with the other 11 (same role, same class) and its cost is one edge.
ruling.clause3: CLOSES: the refusal is evidenced by a measurement — 11/12 have source declarations in the corpus, 1/12 does not.

defectFoundOnTheWay.edge: `qandasetbody` — 1 edge (4 uses collapse into it), file libxslt/tests/docbook/test/qa.xml line 44
defectFoundOnTheWay.whatTheAnalyzerSays: `resolvable: "unresolved"` with `danglingEntityReference: true` — the label calls the document's own entity dangling
defectFoundOnTheWay.whyATreeDump: the pinned grammar parses this file's `doctypedecl` as `<! DOCTYPE Name ExternalID ERROR >`: the entire internal subset — which holds `<!ENTITY qandasetbody "<qandadiv>…">`, a multi-line value containing markup — is an ERROR node. The analyzer never sees a declaration node, so the use is unresolvable TO THE ANALYZER even though the document declares it.
defectFoundOnTheWay.controlsRun: internal subsets parse with 0 ERROR and a `GEDecl` child in the simple shapes (SYSTEM+subset, PUBLIC+subset, bare subset, plain multi-line value); a markup-valued entity triggered ERROR in the synthetic shapes too, so the trigger involves the value's content rather than the DOCTYPE form alone. NOT isolated further — recorded as the grammar limitation it is, with the tree dump as evidence.
defectFoundOnTheWay.classification: grammar limitation, NOT an analyzer defect and NOT a dangling reference. Overturn: a grammar that parses this internal subset would make the declaration readable and the edge `in-document`.
defectFoundOnTheWay.cost: 1 edge of 11,108 references on this population (4 source sites)
